queue.title: Local EIG vs terminal scientific utility audit
Budget-aware terminal value-of-information screen
queue.hypothesis: Full remaining-budget terminal posterior utility aligns intervention choice with terminal causal recovery better than immediate one-step EIG.

checkpoint.note: A local non-atomic attempt completed seed 59001 and then timed out before the next world. Because the preregistration requires atomic per-world persistence, that observation is deliberately not counted and seed 59001 must be rerun from the frozen protocol.
checkpoint.next_action: Run seed 59001 atomically, persist its complete action-level result, then continue sequentially through 59006. Do not pool any unpersisted partial output.

established_findings: Unconditional two-step search does not improve the primary metric after RNG isolation and costs roughly 9x compute.
Historical width-2 breadth showed benefit in an unrecoverable implementation lineage, but that effect cannot be assumed to transfer to benchmark v2.
Simple adaptive breadth thresholds and local-margin depth gates failed prior preregistered validation.
Nonlinear-aware likelihoods improve absolute nonlinear recovery but do not establish a breadth advantage.
A simple model-disagreement proposal bonus worsens recovery prospectively.
A single unmodeled latent common cause can reverse the historical breadth advantage.
Historical EXP-002 runs are not exactly resumable because executable mechanics and per-world seed/state lineage were not persisted.

Fresh benchmark v2 now has a frozen executable engine, exact 29,281-DAG support, budget 15, strict nested breadth, posterior-predictive EIG scoring, isolated RNG namespaces, and a source-addressed manifest.

On benchmark v2, the n=12 breadth screen was directionally favorable but unresolved; the preregistered n=48 replication collapsed to a null primary effect: width2-width1 edge error +0.0140, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.2420,+0.2754], identical 60.4% MAP recovery, and about 2.06x planner simulations. Unconditional width-2 superiority is not supported on benchmark v2.

The benchmark-v2 null is not explained by simple proposal redundancy: the extra swarm supplied the selected action and increased estimated EIG on 55.9% of decisions, yet world-level incremental EIG was essentially unrelated to terminal edge-error benefit (r=-0.064).

EXP-002R5 supports a Monte-Carlo winner's-curse mechanism in the frozen 3-simulation EIG judge: across 61 decisions on 6 fresh worlds, candidate rank correlation with an independent 30-simulation audit was only 0.104; extra-swarm winners had greater optimism than base-swarm winners (world-stratified mean +0.0518 EIG/cost, bootstrap 95% CI [0.0093,0.0986]) and slightly higher misranking (91.4% vs 88.5%). This is diagnostic evidence, not yet evidence that estimator correction improves terminal recovery.

EXP-002R6 falsified compute-matched two-stage EIG racing as the direct fix: on 12 fresh paired worlds racing worsened mean edge error by +0.150 (bootstrap 95% CI [-0.140,+0.421]), worsened Brier and true-DAG mass, despite increasing MAP recovery from 41.7% to 58.3%. This metric split redirects the queue from estimator variance toward local-objective / terminal-utility alignment.

EXP-002R7 does not support a universal local-EIG/terminal mismatch: mean within-world rank alignment to terminal edge recovery was positive (rho 0.238) but highly heterogeneous, ranging from -0.248 to +0.758. The 30-sim EIG argmax averaged rank 5 of 10 and landed in the top three only 33.3%, so state-dependent alignment remains unresolved.

EXP-002R8 prospectively falsified mean posterior edge uncertainty as the proposed alignment moderator: on 12 fixed validation worlds the uncertainty-vs-alignment correlation was -0.174 with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.642,+0.261]. Initial max posterior mass showed a larger positive correlation (+0.484) but its interval crossed zero, so no state gate is established. The queue redirects to objective design rather than thresholding.

EXP-002R9 falsified simple replacement of whole-DAG entropy EIG with edge-marginal entropy utility: mean rank-alignment gain was only +0.077 and improved in 3/6 worlds; both objectives' argmax actions averaged about sixth of ten terminally.

EXP-002R10 falsified simple action-space orthogonalization: unique affordable interventions nearly doubled (5.09 to 9.48 on average) but terminal edge error worsened by +0.292, with only 4/12 paired wins, worse Brier and true-DAG mass, and higher planner simulations. Proposal diversity alone is not the missing mechanism; the queue now audits posterior-predictive calibration.

EXP-002R11 found measurable posterior-predictive intervention-outcome discrepancy but falsified it as the dominant decision-failure mechanism: mean calibration-error correlation with EIG rank error was +0.124 (bootstrap 95% CI [-0.056,+0.301]) and with terminal badness was -0.005 (95% CI [-0.187,+0.200]). High-precision one-step EIG remained weakly aligned with terminal recovery (mean rho +0.188), redirecting the queue to full remaining-budget value-of-information rather than calibration correction.
dynamic_enqueue_rules: Every completed experiment must generate at least one next candidate unless a stronger queued candidate already tests the same uncertainty.
Falsification never empties the queue; it narrows or redirects it.
Do not enqueue equivalent retries without a changed causal hypothesis, state representation, reward, search depth, world model, or evaluation design.
Promote surprising anomalies and control victories into diagnostic experiments.
Maintain matched resource budgets and preserve all negative results.
